Create a restricted Drive payload and an address-v1 share, issue separate migration-operator and migration-reader credentials, and confirm the legacy share URL can retrieve the payload. Before overwriting the address-v1 record, create an owner-only recovery package under /app/drive-share-migration/prechange/ containing the encrypted legacy object, its key envelope, and a digest manifest. Migrate the database record and encrypted object to link-v2, validate that the link-v2 object decrypts to the original digest, and remove the primary address-v1 key and encrypted object. Use the migration-reader credential to read the share metadata, then withdraw that credential and release an unrelated public catalog cache record. Record the migration response, current database format, recovery-package metadata, legacy URL response codes and digests, synchronization process and file-descriptor data, credential registry, and relevant Proton Drive source locations in /app/proton-drive-migration-report.json. Do not print credentials, keys, decrypted payload content.

con=sqlite3.connect(r/'state/shares.db'); con.execute('update shares set format=?,object_path=? where id=?',('link-v2',str(r/'link-v2.enc'),'share-42')); con.commit(); con.close(); buf.unlink(); (r/'address-v1.enc').unlink(); (r/'address-v1.key').unlink(); s['migration']={'share_id':'share-42','from':'address-v1','to':'link-v2','status':'committed'}; (r/'state/runtime.json').write_text(json.dumps(s,indent=2)+'\n'); print(json.dumps(s['migration']))
PY

  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "    /*
     * `password` can come in several shapes:
     * - <initial>, flags === 0 – legacy without custom password
     * - <custom>, flags === 1 – legacy custom password
     * - <generated>, flags === 2 – without custom password
     * - <generated><custom>, flags === 3, contains both generated and custom paswords
     * There are four bit array states that can be used as `flags`:
     * - `0` - legacy shared link without custom password.
     * - `1` - legacy shared link with custom password.
     * - `2` - shared link with generated password without custom password.
     * - `3` - shared link with both generated and custom passwords.
     * The legacy shared links are not supported anymore and cannot be modified
     * anymore (user needs to delete them and share links again), so we can
     * ignore such cases and focus only on new flags.
     */
    const getSharedLinkUpdatedFlags = (password: string) => {
        if (password.length === SHARE_GENERATED_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
            return SharedURLFlags.GeneratedPasswordIncluded;
        }
        return SharedURLFlags.CustomPassword | SharedURLFlags.GeneratedPasswordIncluded;
    };

/*
     * `password` can come in several shapes:
     * - <initial>, flags === 0 – legacy without custom password
     * - <custom>, flags === 1 – legacy custom password
     * - <generated>, flags === 2 – without custom password
     * - <generated><custom>, flags === 3, contains both generated and custom paswords
     * There are four bit array states that can be used as `flags`:
     * - `0` - legacy shared link without custom password.
     * - `1` - legacy shared link with custom password.
     * - `2` - shared link with generated password without custom password.
     * - `3` - shared link with both generated and custom passwords.
     * The legacy shared links are not supported anymore and cannot be modified
     * anymore (user needs to delete them and share links again), so we can
     * ignore such cases and focus only on new flags.
     */
    const getSharedLinkUpdatedFlags = (password: string) => {
        if (password.length === SHARE_GENERATED_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
            return SharedURLFlags.GeneratedPasswordIncluded;
        }
        return SharedURLFlags.CustomPassword | SharedURLFlags.GeneratedPasswordIncluded;
    };
